questions.question: Let $f(x)$ and $g(x)$ be twice differentiable functions satisfying $f''(x) = g''(x)$ for all $x \in \mathbf{R}$, $f'(1) = 2g'(1) = 4$ and $g(2) = 3f(2) = 9$. Then $f(25) - g(25)$ is equal to :
questions.solution:
Given $f''(x) = g''(x)$ for all $x \in \mathbf{R}$.

Let $h(x) = f(x) - g(x)$.

Taking the second derivative, $h''(x) = f''(x) - g''(x) = 0$.

Integrating with respect to $x$, $h'(x) = c_1$.

Given $f'(1) = 4$ and $g'(1) = 2$, $h'(1) = f'(1) - g'(1) = 4 - 2 = 2$.

Therefore, $c_1 = 2$, which gives $h'(x) = 2$.

Integrating again with respect to $x$, $h(x) = 2x + c_2$.

Given $3f(2) = 9 \Rightarrow f(2) = 3$ and $g(2) = 9$, $h(2) = f(2) - g(2) = 3 - 9 = -6$.

Substituting $x = 2$ in $h(x)$, $h(2) = 2(2) + c_2 = -6 \Rightarrow c_2 = -10$.

Thus, $h(x) = 2x - 10$.

Substituting $x = 25$, $h(25) = f(25) - g(25) = 2(25) - 10 = 40$.

Answer: $40$

questions.question: If $∫ \sqrt{sec2x - 1}dx = \alpha{log}_{e}\left|cos2x + \beta + \sqrt{cos2x\left(1 + cos\dfrac{1}{β}x\right)}\right|$   $+$ constant, then $\beta - \alpha$ is equal to ______.
questions.solution:
Given,

$∫ \sqrt{sec2x - 1}dx = \alpha{log}_{e}\left|cos2x + \beta + \sqrt{cos2x\left(1 + cos\dfrac{1}{β}x\right)}\right| + C$

Now solving $L . H . S$ we get,

$∫ \sqrt{sec2x - 1}dx = ∫ \sqrt{\dfrac{1 - cos2x}{cos2x}}dx$

$⇒ ∫ \sqrt{sec2x - 1}dx = \sqrt{2} ∫ \dfrac{sinx}{2{cos}^{2}x - 1}dx$

Now let $cosx = t ⇒ - sinxdx = dt$

$⇒ ∫ \sqrt{sec2x - 1}dx = - \sqrt{2} ∫ \dfrac{dt}{2{t}^{2} - 1}$

$⇒ ∫ \sqrt{sec2x - 1}dx = - ln | \sqrt{2}cosx + \sqrt{cos2x} | + C$

$= - \dfrac{1}{2}ln\left|2{cos}^{2}x + cos2x + 2\sqrt{cos2x} \cdot \sqrt{2}cosx\right| + C$

$= - \dfrac{1}{2}ln\left|cos2x + \dfrac{1}{2} + \sqrt{cos2x} \cdot \sqrt{1 + cos2x}\right| + C$

Now on comparing with $∫ \sqrt{sec2x - 1}dx = \alpha{log}_{e}\left|cos2x + \beta + \sqrt{cos2x\left(1 + cos\dfrac{1}{β}x\right)}\right| + C$

We get, $\beta = \dfrac{1}{2}, \alpha = - \dfrac{1}{2} ⇒ \beta - \alpha = 1$

questions.question: Let $I\left(x\right) = ∫ \sqrt{\dfrac{x + 7}{x}}dx$ and $I\left(9\right) = 12 + 7{log}_{e}7$. If $I\left(1\right) = \alpha + 7{log}_{e}\left(1 + 2\sqrt{2}\right),$ then ${α}^{4}$ is equal to _____.
questions.solution:
Given,

$I\left(x\right) = ∫ \sqrt{\dfrac{x + 7}{x}}dx$

Now let, $\dfrac{x + 7}{x} = {t}^{2} ⇒ - \dfrac{7}{x2}dx = 2tdt$

$⇒ dx = \dfrac{- 14t}{\left({t}^{2} - 1\right)2}dt$

So, $I\left(x\right) = - 14 ∫ \dfrac{t2}{\left({t}^{2} - 1\right)2}dt$

$⇒ I\left(x\right) = - 14 ∫ dt\left({t}^{2} + \dfrac{1}{t2} - 2\right)$

$⇒ I\left(x\right) = \dfrac{- 14}{2} ∫ \left[\left(1 - \dfrac{1}{t2}\right)\left(t + \dfrac{1}{t}\right)2 - 4 + \left(1 + \dfrac{1}{t2}\right)\left(t - \dfrac{1}{t}\right)2\right]dt$

$⇒ I\left(x\right) = - 7\left(\dfrac{1}{4}ln\left|\dfrac{t + \dfrac{1}{t} - 2}{t + \dfrac{1}{t} + 2}\right| - \dfrac{1}{t - \dfrac{1}{t}}\right) + c$

Now when $x = 9, t = \dfrac{4}{3}$

$⇒ I\left(9\right) = 12 + 7 \times ln7 = \dfrac{- 7}{4}ln\left(\dfrac{1}{7}\right)2 + 7 \times \dfrac{12}{7} + c$

$⇒ c = \dfrac{7}{2}ln7$

Now when $x = 1, t = 2\sqrt{2}$

$⇒ I\left(1\right) = + \dfrac{7}{4}ln\left(\dfrac{2\sqrt{2} + 1}{2\sqrt{2} - 1}\right)2 + 7 \times \dfrac{2\sqrt{2}}{7} + \dfrac{7}{2}ln7$

$⇒ I\left(1\right) = \dfrac{7}{2}ln\left(\dfrac{\left(2\sqrt{2} + 1\right)2}{7}\right) + 2\sqrt{2} + \dfrac{7}{2}ln7$

$⇒ I\left(1\right) = 7ln\left(2\sqrt{2} + 1\right) - \dfrac{7}{2}ln7 + 2\sqrt{2} + \dfrac{7}{2}ln7$

$⇒ \alpha = 2\sqrt{2} ⇒ {α}^{4} = 64$

Let $\dfrac{x + 2}{x - 1} = t$

Differentiate on both sides

$\dfrac{\left(x - 1\right) - \left(x + 2\right)}{\left(x - 1\right)2} . dx = dt$

$⇒ \dfrac{dx}{\left(x - 1\right)2} = \dfrac{- dt}{3}$

$= \dfrac{4}{3}t\dfrac{- 1}{4} + C$

$= \dfrac{4}{3}\left(\dfrac{1}{t}\right)\dfrac{1}{4} + C$

$= \dfrac{4}{3}\left(\dfrac{x - 1}{x + 2}\right)\dfrac{1}{4} + C$

questions.solution:
Given,

$I\left(x\right) = ∫ \dfrac{x + 1}{x\left(1 + x{e}^{x}\right)2}dx$

Now let $1 + x{e}^{x} = t$

$⇒ {e}^{x}\left(x + 1\right)dx = dt$

So, $I\left(x\right) = ∫ \dfrac{1}{\left(t - 1\right){t}^{2}}dt$

$⇒ I\left(x\right) = ∫ \dfrac{\left(1 - {t}^{2}\right) + {t}^{2}}{\left(t - 1\right){t}^{2}}dt$

$⇒ I\left(x\right) = ∫ \dfrac{- \left(t + 1\right)}{t2} + \dfrac{1}{t - 1}dt$

$⇒ I\left(x\right) = ∫ - \dfrac{1}{t} - \dfrac{1}{t2} + \dfrac{1}{t - 1}dt$

$⇒ I\left(x\right) = - lnt + \dfrac{1}{t} + ln\left(t - 1\right) + C$

$⇒ I\left(x\right) = ln\left(\dfrac{x{e}^{x}}{x{e}^{x} + 1}\right) + \dfrac{1}{x{e}^{x} + 1} + C$

Also given,$\lim_{x \to \infty}I\left(x\right) = 0$

$⇒ \lim_{x \to \infty}I\left(x\right) = \lim_{x \to \infty}\left[ln\left(1 - \dfrac{1}{x{e}^{x} + 1}\right) + \dfrac{1}{x{e}^{x} + 1} + C\right]$

$⇒ \lim_{x \to \infty}I\left(x\right) = \left[ln\left(1 - 0\right) + 0 + C\right]$

$⇒ C = 0$

Now finding,

$I\left(1\right) = ln\left(\dfrac{e}{e + 1}\right) + \dfrac{1}{e + 1} = 1 + \dfrac{1}{e + 1} - ln ( e + 1 )$

$⇒ I\left(1\right) = \dfrac{e + 2}{e + 1} - ln\left(e + 1\right)$

$= ∫ \dfrac{\left(\dfrac{3}{2} - \dfrac{1}{2}\right)\left(cosx - sinx\right)}{sin\dfrac{π}{3} + sin2x}dx$

$∫ \dfrac{sinx}{{sin}^{3}x + {cos}^{3}x}dx = \alpha{log}_{e} | 1 + tanx | + \beta{log}_{e}\left|1 - tanx + {tan}^{2}x\right| + \gamma{tan}^{- 1}\left(\dfrac{2tanx - 1}{3}\right) + C, . . . . . . . . . . \left(i\right)$

Let, $I = ∫ \dfrac{sinx}{{sin}^{3}x + {cos}^{3}x}dx$
$I = ∫ \dfrac{tanx{sec}^{2}x}{{tan}^{3} + 1}dx$

Put $tanx = t ⇒ {sec}^{2}xdx = dt$

$= ∫ \dfrac{tdt}{{t}^{3} + 1} = ∫ \dfrac{t}{( t + 1 ) \left({t}^{2} - t + 1\right)}dt$
Now $\dfrac{t}{( t + 1 ) \left({t}^{2} - t + 1\right)} = \dfrac{A}{t + 1} + \dfrac{Bt + C}{{t}^{2} - t + 1}$

$t = A\left({t}^{2} - t + 1\right) + ( Bt + C ) ( t + 1 )$

$t = {t}^{2}\left(A + B\right) - t\left(A - B - C\right) + A + C$

Comparing on both sides

$A + B = 0, - A + B + C = 1, A + C = 0$

Solving these equations
$A = - \dfrac{1}{3}, B = \dfrac{1}{3}, C = \dfrac{1}{3}$
Hence $I = ∫ \left\{\dfrac{- \dfrac{1}{3}}{t + 1} + \dfrac{1}{3}\left(\dfrac{t + 1}{{t}^{2} - t + 1}\right)\right\}dt$
$= - \dfrac{1}{3} ∫ 1\left(t + 1\right)dt + \dfrac{1}{3} ∫ \dfrac{\dfrac{1}{2}\left(2t - 1\right) + \dfrac{3}{2}}{{t}^{2} - t + 1}dt$

$= - \dfrac{1}{3} ∫ 1\left(t + 1\right)dt + \dfrac{1}{6} ∫ 2t - 1\left({t}^{2} - t + 1\right) + \dfrac{1}{2} ∫ \dfrac{dt}{\left(t - \dfrac{1}{2}\right)2 + \left(\dfrac{3}{2}\right)2}$$= - \dfrac{1}{3}ln\left|t + 1\right| + \dfrac{1}{6}ln\left|{t}^{2} - t + 1\right| + \dfrac{1}{2} \cdot \dfrac{2}{3}{tan}^{- 1}\left(\dfrac{2t - 1}{3}\right) + C$

From equation $\left(i\right)$, Comparing from both sides
$⇒ \alpha = - \dfrac{1}{3}, \beta = \dfrac{1}{6}$ and $\gamma = \dfrac{1}{3}$
So $18\left(\alpha + \beta + {γ}^{2}\right)$

$= 18\left(- \dfrac{1}{3} + \dfrac{1}{6} + \dfrac{1}{3}\right)$

$= 3$

questions.solution:
Let, $I = ∫ \dfrac{sin\dfrac{3}{2}x + cos\dfrac{3}{2}x}{{sin}^{3}x{cos}^{3}xsin ( x - \theta )}dx$

$⇒ I = ∫ \dfrac{sin\dfrac{3}{2}x + cos\dfrac{3}{2}x}{{sin}^{3}x{cos}^{3}x ( sinxcos\theta - cosxsin\theta )}dx$

$⇒ I = ∫ \dfrac{sin\dfrac{3}{2}x + cos\dfrac{3}{2}x}{{sin}^{3}x{cos}^{4}x ( tanxcos\theta - sin\theta )}dx$

$⇒ I = ∫ \dfrac{sin\dfrac{3}{2}x}{sin\dfrac{3}{2}x{cos}^{2}x\sqrt{tanxcos\theta - sin\theta}}dx + ∫ \dfrac{cos\dfrac{3}{2}x}{{sin}^{2}xcos\dfrac{3}{2}x\sqrt{cos\theta - cotxsin\theta}}dx$

$⇒ I = ∫ \dfrac{1}{{cos}^{2}x\sqrt{tanxcos\theta - sin\theta}}dx + ∫ \dfrac{1}{{sin}^{2}x\sqrt{cos\theta - cotxsin\theta}}dx$

$⇒ I = ∫ \dfrac{{sec}^{2}x}{tanxcos\theta - sin\theta}dx + ∫ \dfrac{{cosec}^{2}x}{cos\theta - cotxsin\theta}dx$

So, $I = {I}_{1} + {I}_{2} . . . . \left\{let\right\}$

For ${I}_{1}$, let $tanxcos\theta - sin\theta = {t}^{2}$

$⇒ cos\theta \times {sec}^{2}xdx = 2tdt$

$⇒ {sec}^{2}xdx = \dfrac{2tdt}{cos\theta}$

For ${I}_{2}$, let $cos\theta - cotxsin\theta = {z}^{2}$

$⇒ {cosec}^{2}x \times sin\thetadx = 2zdz$

$⇒ {cosec}^{2}xdx = \dfrac{2zdz}{sin\theta}$

$⇒ I = ∫ \dfrac{2tdt}{cos\theta \times t} + ∫ \dfrac{2zdz}{sin\theta \times z}$

$⇒ I = 2\left[\left(sec\theta\right) ∫ \left(1\right)dt + cosec\theta ∫ \left(1\right)dz\right]$

$⇒ I = 2sec\theta\sqrt{tanxcos\theta - sin\theta} + 2 cosec \theta\sqrt{cos\theta - cotxsin\theta}$

$⇒ A \times B = 4sec\thetacosec\theta$

$⇒ A \times B = \dfrac{2}{2} \times \dfrac{4}{sin\thetacos\theta}$

$⇒ A \times B = 8 cosec 2\theta$

Let, $- {x}^{2} = t ⇒ xdx = - \dfrac{1}{2}dt$

By using integrating by parts, i.e. $∫ \left(u \cdot v\right)dx = u ∫ vdx - ∫ \left[\dfrac{d}{dx}u ∫ vdx\right]dx + c,$ we get

$I = - \dfrac{1}{2}\left[{t}^{2} ∫ {e}^{t}dt - ∫ \left(2t ∫ {e}^{t}dt\right)dt\right] + c$

$⇒ I = - \dfrac{1}{2}\left[{t}^{2}{e}^{t} - 2 ∫ t{e}^{t}dt\right] + c$

Again, applying integrating by parts, we get

$⇒ I = - \dfrac{1}{2}\left[{t}^{2}{e}^{t} - 2\left(t ∫ {e}^{t}dt - ∫ 1 \cdot {e}^{t}dt\right)\right] + c$

$⇒ I = - \dfrac{1}{2}\left[{t}^{2}{e}^{t} - 2\left(t{e}^{t} - {e}^{t}\right)\right] + c$

$⇒ I = - \dfrac{1}{2}\left[{t}^{2}{e}^{t} - 2t{e}^{t} + 2{e}^{t}\right] + c$

$⇒ I = - \dfrac{et}{2}\left[{t}^{2} - 2t + 2\right] + c$

questions.question: Let $f(x) = \int \left(\dfrac{16x + 24}{x^2 + 2x - 15}\right) dx$. If $f(4) = 14 \log_e(3)$ and $f(7) = \log_e(2^{\alpha} \cdot 3^{\beta})$, $\alpha, \beta \in \mathbb{N}$, then $\alpha + \beta$ is equal to:
questions.solution:
The given integral is $f(x) = \int \left(\dfrac{16x + 24}{x^2 + 2x - 15}\right) dx$.

Factorizing the denominator, we get $x^2 + 2x - 15 = (x + 5)(x - 3)$.

Using partial fractions, we can write:

$\dfrac{16x + 24}{(x + 5)(x - 3)} = \dfrac{A}{x + 5} + \dfrac{B}{x - 3}$

$16x + 24 = A(x - 3) + B(x + 5)$

Substituting $x = 3$, we get $72 = 8B \Rightarrow B = 9$.

Substituting $x = -5$, we get $-56 = -8A \Rightarrow A = 7$.

Therefore, the integral becomes:

$f(x) = \int \left(\dfrac{7}{x + 5} + \dfrac{9}{x - 3}\right) dx$

$f(x) = 7 \log_e|x + 5| + 9 \log_e|x - 3| + C$

Given $f(4) = 14 \log_e(3)$, we substitute $x = 4$:

$f(4) = 7 \log_e(9) + 9 \log_e(1) + C = 14 \log_e(3) + C$

Since $f(4) = 14 \log_e(3)$, we get $C = 0$.

Thus, $f(x) = 7 \log_e|x + 5| + 9 \log_e|x - 3|$.

Now, substituting $x = 7$:

$f(7) = 7 \log_e(12) + 9 \log_e(4)$

$f(7) = 7 \log_e(2^2 \cdot 3) + 9 \log_e(2^2)$

$f(7) = 7(2 \log_e(2) + \log_e(3)) + 18 \log_e(2)$

$f(7) = 14 \log_e(2) + 7 \log_e(3) + 18 \log_e(2)$

$f(7) = 32 \log_e(2) + 7 \log_e(3)$

$f(7) = \log_e(2^{32} \cdot 3^7)$

Comparing this with $f(7) = \log_e(2^{\alpha} \cdot 3^{\beta})$, we get $\alpha = 32$ and $\beta = 7$.

Therefore, $\alpha + \beta = 32 + 7 = 39$.

Answer: $39$
